Bhṛgusaṁhitā
(‘a collection [made by] भृगु’)
------------------------------------------
Hindu अस्त्रोलोग्य् accepts and bases its calculations on the twelve rāśis (signs of the Zodiac) and nine ग्रहस् or प्लनेत्स् (including राहु and केतु). There is a popular belief that a work called Bhṛgu-saṁhitā exists, in which the readings of all possible horoscopes got by the permutation and combination of these twelve rāśis and nine ग्रहस् are given. By just referring to the particular होरोस्चोपे given there with ours, we can know everything about our past, present and future.
Some scholars have calculated that a complete Bhṛgusaṁhitā would have to contain 7,46,49,000 horoscopes and at least ten times this number, of ślokas, assuming a minimum of ten ślokas per होरोस्चोपे.
The book itself has not been found. Here and there, some astrologers claim to possess parts or the whole of the work which is hard to believe. It is extremely difficult, if not impossible, to accommodate such a voluminous work even in a big library.

Bhṛgu
(‘the roaster’)
------------------------------------------
‘Bhṛgu’ is a well-known name that appears in several works, both Vedic and Paurāṇic. Assuming that the word has been derived from the root ‘bhṛj’ or ‘bhrāj’ (‘to burn or to roast’) it could have been the name of the fire-priest by whose magical power the altar fire was kindled. According to a myth, god Mātariśvan brought lightning from the heavens to this earth and taught the art of kindling fire with araṇis or fire-sticks, to the Bhṛgus (‘bhārgavāḥ’), the Āṇgirasas and the Atharvans.
The sage भृगु has been described as the mānasaputra or mindborn son of ब्रह्मा, the Creator. Sometimes he has been stated to be the son of god वरुण or even of इन्द्र. He was the ड़थेर् of लक्ष्मी the spouse of विष्णु. (Hence the name ‘Bhārgavī’ has been applied to her.) In other incarnations he was the ड़थेर् of शुक्राचार्य (the गुरु of the असुरस् or demons) and of sages like च्यवन. He is said to have once tested the Trinity—Brahmā, विष्णु and Śiva—and come to the conclusion that विष्णु was the best among them and that he alone deserved worship.
He is one of the well-known sages who were ‘gotra-pravartakas,’ originators of gotras or lineage. Hence his descendants are called ‘Bhārgavas.’ Sages जमदग्नि and परशुराम belonged to this गोत्र.
The Mahābhārata pictures him as a great savant often delivering discourses on abstruse matters.
He was one of the four sages—the other three being मरीचि, अत्रि and Kaśyapa—who elaborated the वैखानस आगम precepts followed by some Vaiṣṇava sects.
The place where भृगु is said to have performed austerities is known as भृगु-Kaccha. It is situated on the bank of the river नर्मदा near its confluence with the sea. It is now known as Broach, situated in the Gujarat State. At the place known as the Daśāśvamedha Ghāṭ, the king बलि is said to have performed the horse sacrifice. It was here that he propitiated वामन (the dwarf-इन्चर्नतिओन् of विष्णु) and granted him the boon of ‘land covered in three steps.’ The city itself is considered to be very ancient, the original ‘Bhṛgupura’ (city of भृगु) being built by भृगु himself.
